resources.string: SoundPeter talks to your earbuds over Bluetooth, and Android asks you to allow that. It is the only permission the app uses.
Without Bluetooth access the app cannot reach your earbuds.
Pick your SoundPEATS earbuds. Close PeatsAudio first: only one app can hold the controls.
No SoundPEATS earbuds paired. Pair them in the Bluetooth settings first.
No account. No internet. Nothing leaves this phone.
Could not reach the controls of %1$s. Close PeatsAudio if it is open, check the earbuds are connected for audio, then try again.
Bluetooth access is turned off for SoundPeter.
Turn LDAC off to use this
On these earbuds LDAC and two devices take turns: turning one off turns the other on. The earbuds reconnect each time, which takes a few seconds.

SoundPeter does not support the equalizer for these earbuds yet. If you want to change EQ settings, you can contribute to the project by tapping the button below. It takes a few minutes with the official PeatsAudio app.
These earbuds cannot report their EQ, and this phone has not set one on them yet. Pick a profile or move a band to set it.
Presets are fixed curves. Pick Stock, New or one of your own profiles to set bands one by one.
Equalizer curve. Pick a band below to change it.
Added the profile from the file.
That file is not a SoundPeter profile for these earbuds.
The profile is removed from this phone. The earbuds keep the sound they have now.
0 dB on every band is the earbuds\' own tuning. The earbuds cannot report their EQ, so each time SoundPeter connects it puts back the one this phone last set, as the official app does.
When off, the earbuds ignore taps and holds.
Every tap and hold goes back to what the earbuds came with.
These earbuds did not report any touch controls.
Take the earbuds out of your ears first. The beep is loud.
Check that each ear tip seals well. A good seal gives fuller bass and better noise cancelling.
Put both earbuds in your ears and stay still somewhere quiet. The earbuds play a short sound and check how well each ear tip seals. It takes about 10 seconds.
Noise control turns off for the test and back on afterwards.
For an earbud with a poor fit, push it in a little further and twist it slightly so the tip seals, then test again. If it still does not fit, try a larger ear tip.
No result came back. Check that both earbuds are connected and in your ears, then try again.
Plays a series of sounds for about 30 seconds to push water out of the speakers, for example after rain or a workout. Take the earbuds out of your ears first.
Draining. The earbuds stop by themselves after about 30 seconds.
Uses Bluetooth LE Audio where the phone supports it. The earbuds restart to switch and reconnect by themselves.

SoundPeter learns what a model can do, and its equalizer, from what the official PeatsAudio app reads from the earbuds and sends to them. Android can log that, and one recording per model is enough to add it for everyone.
Turn on Developer options: in Settings, open About phone and tap Build number seven times. On Samsung it is under About phone, Software information.
In Settings, Developer options, set Bluetooth HCI snoop log to Enabled (not Filtered). Then turn Bluetooth off and on.

Open PeatsAudio with these earbuds connected. Open each of its screens once without changing anything, so it reads every setting, and run its fit test if it has one. Then on its EQ screen tap SOUNDPEATS Classic and every other preset once, a few seconds apart. Do not come back to SoundPeter yet.
Back in Developer options, tap Take bug report, then Full report.
It takes several minutes, and Android shows nothing while it works. Wait for the notification that says it is ready.
When the notification says the bug report is ready, tap it and share it to SoundPeter. If you miss the notification, tap Choose a bug report below, open the menu and pick Bug reports to find it.
SoundPeter shows what it found. Name the EQ curves in the order you tapped them, then send the report. If SoundPeter is connected to the same earbuds, its own device report goes in too.
Afterwards, set Bluetooth HCI snoop log back to Disabled and delete the bug report. It holds a lot of personal data.
Reading the bug report. This can take a minute.

SoundPeter reads the bug report only on this phone. From the Bluetooth log inside it, it reads only the messages exchanged with SoundPEATS earbuds and skips everything else. It does not keep the file. Nothing is sent to any server until you send the report yourself, which opens GitHub in your browser. SoundPeter has no internet access at all: its app info in Android lists no network permission.
This bug report has no Bluetooth log. Set Bluetooth HCI snoop log to Enabled, turn Bluetooth off and on, use PeatsAudio again, then take a new bug report.
The Bluetooth log in this bug report has nothing from SoundPEATS earbuds. Check that the snoop log was set to Enabled, not Filtered, and Bluetooth turned off and on, before you used PeatsAudio.
That file is not a bug report.

resources.string: Not in the log. Turning Bluetooth off and on before opening PeatsAudio records it. The report is still useful without it.
A model SoundPeter does not know yet (%1$s)
SoundPeter\'s own device report for these earbuds goes in too.
To add SoundPeter\'s own device report as well, connect these earbuds in SoundPeter before sending.
No EQ curves in this recording. The settings are still worth sending.
Name at least one curve to send the report.

Nothing has left this phone yet. Send on GitHub copies the report and opens a new issue with it filled in, in your browser. It is sent only when you submit the issue there. If the issue is empty, paste the report into it.
Copied. If the new issue on GitHub is empty, paste the report into it, then submit it.
Copied. Paste it into a device report issue on the project page to help support these earbuds.
Every setting on the earbuds goes back to how it left the factory. They may also forget this phone; then pair them again in the Bluetooth settings.
